skill.name: agent-browser
skill.description: Browser automation skill for AI agents using inference.sh. It documents page navigation, element interaction, screenshots, video recording, proxy settings, file upload, and JavaScript execution through the agent-browser app.
skill.summary: Automates browser sessions with navigation, interaction, screenshots, recording, and extraction workflows.
skill.author: inferencesh

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, shell helper templates, and placeholder URLs. I confirmed the remote pipe-to-shell installer, SOCKS proxy support, and a semantic risk where the authentication guide extracts and logs session cookies.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell quick start with a package manager, checksum-verified download, or a command that asks users to inspect the script first.

remediation.issue: Authentication guide extracts and prints session cookies.
remediation.suggestion: Remove cookie logging examples, redact session data by default, and document that cookie export is only for authorized debugging.

remediation.issue: SOCKS proxy examples include privacy and anonymity routing.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit acceptable-use limits and remove framing that suggests bypassing site, corporate, or network controls.

remediation.issue: Shell templates interpolate user input into JSON strings.
remediation.suggestion: Build request JSON with jq --arg or another JSON encoder so URLs and form values cannot alter request structure.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Sessions With Agent Browser
content.value_statement: Manual browser workflows slow down research, testing, and data capture. Agent Browser gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured commands for browsing, interacting, and collecting page evidence.
actual_capabilities: Open web pages and return current URL, title, screenshot, and element refs.
Interact with elements using refs for clicks, form fills, key presses, scrolling, drag and drop, and file upload.
Refresh snapshots after navigation or page changes so agents can use current element refs.
Capture viewport or full page screenshots and record browser sessions for review.
Run JavaScript in the page context to extract text, links, counts, and other DOM data.
Configure viewport, user agent, proxy settings, and authenticated browser workflows.
limitations: The skill depends on the inference.sh CLI and the hosted agent-browser app.
Element refs can expire after navigation, form submission, or dynamic page updates.
Authenticated workflows require user-provided credentials and careful secret handling.
JavaScript execution and proxy use can create security or policy risk on sensitive sites.

use_cases.title: Verify Web Forms
use_cases.description: Open a form, inspect element refs, submit test data, and capture screenshots that prove the result.

use_cases.title: Collect Page Evidence
use_cases.description: Visit pages, extract visible text and links, and save screenshots for a repeatable research trail.

use_cases.title: Automate Authenticated Checks
use_cases.description: Log in to an approved application, navigate protected pages, and confirm expected dashboard content.

prompt_templates.title: Open and Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Agent Browser to open the target URL, summarize the page title, list visible interactive elements, and note which refs look useful.

prompt_templates.title: Capture Screenshots and Text
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the URL, take a full page screenshot, extract the visible body text, and report the saved evidence items.

prompt_templates.title: Complete a Test Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the form page, identify the field refs, fill the approved test values, submit the form, refresh the snapshot, and describe the result.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Authenticated Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved credentials from environment variables, log in, avoid recording sensitive steps, navigate to the target page, extract the required non-secret data, and close the session.

output_examples.input: Open a product page and capture visible evidence.
output_examples.output: The browser session opened the page, identified the main action buttons, captured a full page screenshot, and extracted the visible product details.

output_examples.input: Submit a contact form with approved test data.
output_examples.output: The workflow filled the requested fields, clicked the submit button, refreshed the page state, and found a confirmation message.

output_examples.input: Check an authenticated dashboard after login.
output_examples.output: The session used the provided credentials, reached the dashboard, confirmed the expected heading, and closed without recording sensitive steps.

best_practices: Refresh the snapshot after navigation, submissions, or dynamic content changes.
Use environment variables or a secrets manager for credentials, and avoid logging sensitive values.
Close every browser session when work is complete to limit lingering authenticated state.
anti_patterns: Do not run browser automation against sites where you lack permission.
Do not record videos or screenshots while entering passwords, tokens, or private user data.
Do not use proxy settings to bypass access controls, rate limits, or site policy.

faq.question: What does Agent Browser automate?
faq.answer: It opens web pages, returns element refs, interacts with page controls, captures screenshots, records sessions, and extracts page data.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Why do element refs stop working?
faq.answer: Refs are tied to the current page state. Take a new snapshot after navigation, form submission, or dynamic content updates.

faq.question: Can it handle login flows?
faq.answer: Yes, but credentials should come from secure sources, and sensitive sessions should not be recorded or logged.

faq.question: Can it run JavaScript on a page?
faq.answer: Yes. Use this only on approved pages because page scripts can expose sensitive DOM content or session data.

faq.question: Does it require external services?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses the inference.sh CLI and the agent-browser app, so network access and an authenticated account may be required.
